summary: Susumu Yamaguchi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University, and under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as professor at Otani University (1934–1964) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Toronto. He founded and served as president of the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Suzanne Karpelès studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at the EFEO (1922–1941) and was first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925).

Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the Open University and King's College London, where she was honorary director of Inform.

Sven Hedin worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his education at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa.

Swami Dayananda Saraswati was an Indologist and philosopher of religion. He studied at Bangalore Sanskrit College and under teachers including Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tarananda Giri.
Swami Lakshman Joo worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933 and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.
Swami Satyananda Puri was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta, where he also held an academic post.

Swami Sivananda Saraswati was active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Thanjavur Medical College and later founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Swami Vimalananda was active in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.

Swami Vivekananda was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and studied under Ramakrishna from around 1881 to 1886.

Sydney Frank Markham was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Wadham College from circa 1920 to 1923. He later served as Secretary and subsequently President of the Museums Association between 1929 and 1942.

Syed Ali Bilgrami was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and the University of London. He served the Government of Hyderabad before becoming Reader in Marathi at Cambridge in 1901.
Syed Ameer Ali was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta, where he subsequently held a post from around 1873 to 1881.
Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist who studied at Langat Singh College and Patna University. He later served as the Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali worked in history and archaeology. He held posts as Principal at Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, both attested in 1932.
Sylvain Brocquet is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Marie-Claude Porcher, and he held an academic post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and occupied the Chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1894 to 1935.
Søren Sørensen was an Indologist who held a post at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and later served at the University of Copenhagen from around 1887 to 1902.
